title: Invariant multiplicities in finite biproducts of a hom-orthogonal family
statement: Let $C$ be an additive category [def-weil-additive-category], let $I$ be a type, and let $s:I\to C$ be hom-orthogonal: for distinct $i,j$, the set of morphisms $s(i)\to s(j)$ is a subsingleton. Suppose each endomorphism ring $\operatorname{End}(s(i))$ has invariant basis number, meaning that an isomorphism between finite free modules of ranks $a,b$ implies $a=b$. For finite types $A,B$, maps $f:A\to I$, $g:B\to I$, and an isomorphism $\bigoplus_{a\in A}s(f(a))\simeq\bigoplus_{b\in B}s(g(b))$, there is a bijection $e:A\simeq B$ with $g(e(a))=f(a)$ for every $a$.

source.place: Elementary invariant-rank argument accompanying Example 3.1; generic finite-biproduct multiplicity theorem implemented by Mathlib CategoryTheory/Preadditive/HomOrthogonal.lean, theorem equiv_of_iso, lines 201–218.

proof.text: Apply the exact Mathlib theorem CategoryTheory.HomOrthogonal.equiv_of_iso. Its proof takes the block-diagonal matrix decompositions of the isomorphism and its inverse. matrixDecomposition_comp and matrixDecomposition_id give inverse rectangular matrices in each endomorphism ring. Matrix.square_of_invertible, using the assumed invariant basis number, gives equal cardinalities of the fibres of f and g. Equiv.ofPreimageEquiv assembles the fibrewise equivalences into a bijection of the full finite index types, preserving their labels. Empty fibres are included.
